analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/developer/build.md (Last-updated date, CI Runner Routing section) and docs/developer/test.md (date, CI runner wording, routing test description). No provider source, protocol, key custody, attestation or authorization code is touched, so TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011 (A-015/A-016/A-017) and the T-052..T-058 controls are unchanged.

The docs describe a CI routing change: ci.yml provider and cluster test jobs (test-provider shards, test-provider-sdk, test-cluster-*, test-cluster-focused) may now run on Darkbloom Sandbox runners via the platform's POST /v1/ci/routes grant, falling back to Blacksmith macOS-27. Any security effect lives in the workflows, not in these docs, and I could not review it. Mitigations stated in the docs: routing off by default (DARKBLOOM_ROUTING must equal 'on'), no routing for fork PRs, grants only if exact labels match, route job has no token permissions or checkout, errors keep the fallback, and the jobs are read-only. Release, signing, publication, model registration, review automation and master/dispatched cache warming stay on literal Blacksmith labels (build.md lines ~295-302). The test.md sentence 'keeps release workflows and the macOS jobs of ci.yml on literal Blacksmith runners' was narrowed to 'release workflows' only, consistent with the new routing of macOS test jobs.

Open integration questions, outside this docs-only batch: (1) the actual .github/workflows/ci.yml and darkbloom-route.yml should confirm that routed test jobs hold no signing, release or secret credentials and that pushes of admitted branches save caches only from routed lanes; (2) GitHub Actions cache sharing between Darkbloom Sandbox and other runners (build.md 'CI Caching') could allow cache poisoning if untrusted code on a sandbox can save to a cache that release lanes restore. The docs say only master/dev pushes save caches and that release lanes use their own keys. No concrete regression is evidenced in the supplied text.
